steps.title: Use the roots to write f(x) in factors

lines.text: The curve crosses the $x$-axis at $-2$ and $3$, so $(x + 2)$ and $(x - 3)$ are factors. The curve opens downwards, so the leading coefficient is negative.
The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=-1$ and $x=3$, so $(x+1)$ and $(x-3)$ are factors.

steps.title: Find the height of bar A

lines.text: A bar is a cylinder, so $V = \pi r^2 h$ with $r = 1$.
The heights form an arithmetic sequence with $a = 71.3$ and, from part (i), $T_5 = 107.3$.

skill.title: Decide if a sequence is arithmetic, geometric or neither

note: Use the SAME method as the references (they are the lesson so far); change one thing, as usual. The method: Test consecutive terms for a common difference or common ratio to classify the sequence. Earlier backups were dropped for doing this instead: Sets two common differences equal and solves an exponential equation for k via a quadratic in y, instead of classifying a sequence.

steps.title: Find the differences between consecutive terms

lines.text: The difference is the same each time, so the sequence is arithmetic with common difference $d = -3$.
The ratio is the same constant for every $n$, so $a_n$ is geometric with common ratio $\frac{1}{5}$.
